report_title: EY Four Trends Redefining Cash Management
executive_summary: The cash management landscape is undergoing a rapid transformation, shifting from transaction-oriented products to strategic, data-driven services. Banks are presented with a compelling opportunity to enrich their value propositions by expanding their portfolios and strengthening client relationships through tailored offerings. Key drivers include the adoption of advanced technologies like AI/ML and the emergence of digital assets such as stablecoins and tokenized funds. This evolution necessitates banks to embrace automation, data-driven insights, industry-specific solutions, and blockchain infrastructure to remain relevant and competitive in the future of corporate, commercial, and small business banking.

key_stats.statistic: 73% of survey respondents say digitizing treasury functions is a challenge.
44% will use managed services from banks to address the challenges of digitization.
90% of CFOs and treasurers want an AI financial advisor that makes recommendations in response to financial issues.
92% of corporate treasurers are comfortable using sector-specific platforms tailored to their industry's unique needs.
71% of survey respondents say there is a lack of suitable sector-centric tools to address their unique financial situation.
>75% of institutional investors expect to increase their allocations to digital assets in 2025.
59% of institutional investors will allocate more than 5% of assets under management (AuM) to digital assets or related products.

themes.name: Treasury Automation to Business Intelligence
themes.description: Cash management is evolving beyond mere process efficiency to deliver strategic business intelligence. This involves leveraging virtual account structures, AI-based forecasting models, and algorithmic liquidity engines to centralize visibility, optimize liquidity, and automate intercompany movements. The goal is to provide treasurers with early warnings on funding gaps and surplus liquidity, enabling more informed and confident short-term investment decisions.
themes.key_stat: 73% of survey respondents say digitizing treasury functions is a challenge.

themes.name: Data-Driven Services for Strategic Advice
themes.description: Banks are redefining their role by moving from transactional processing to becoming strategic advisors, utilizing high-value internal and external data. This includes integrating macroeconomic indicators, supply chain disruptions, and sector benchmarks to offer proactive insights and actionable recommendations. The aim is to help clients anticipate liquidity risks, optimize cash positions, and inform funding and investment decisions, fostering long-term partnerships.
themes.key_stat: 90% of CFOs and treasurers want an AI financial advisor that makes recommendations in response to financial issues.

themes.name: Industry-Specific Solutions as Standard
themes.description: Clients increasingly demand cash management services tailored to their specific industry dynamics, rather than generic financial products. Banks are developing verticalized solutions that combine technology, data-driven insights, and embedded human expertise. These offerings address unique risk triggers, regulatory workflows, and payment needs pertinent to each sector, enhancing relevance and deepening wallet share.
themes.key_stat: 92% of corporate treasurers are comfortable using sector-specific platforms tailored to their industry's unique needs.

themes.name: Blockchain Infrastructure for Value Exchange
themes.description: The growing adoption of digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits, coupled with increasing regulatory clarity, presents new growth opportunities. Blockchain market infrastructure enables new methods of value exchange, enhancing collateralization, reconciliation, and settlement processes. Banks can expand their client base by serving digital-native firms and integrating digital assets into their cash management solutions, streamlining cross-border payments and trade finance.
themes.key_stat: >75% of institutional investors expect to increase their allocations to digital assets in 2025.

key_actions.action: Optimize cash management solutions for specific sectors to differentiate and boost client engagement and loyalty.
key_actions.rationale: The report highlights that 92% of corporate treasurers are comfortable with sector-specific platforms, yet 71% perceive a lack of suitable tools. Tailoring CMIplus offerings to key CEE industries will directly address this gap, providing a significant competitive advantage and strengthening relationships with large international corporates.

key_actions.action: Promote collaboration among IT and business leaders to build new cash management and robo-treasury solutions, leveraging AI/ML.
key_actions.rationale: AI-based forecasting and algorithmic liquidity engines are critical for the evolution towards business intelligence and data-driven services. CMIplus must foster strong internal collaboration and potentially external partnerships to integrate these advanced capabilities, enhancing real-time insights and automation for corporate treasuries.
key_actions.timeline: Ongoing / Short-to-Medium Term (3-12 months for initial pilots)

key_actions.action: Assess opportunities to partner with managed services providers and other third parties to build the foundation for robo-treasury, TaaS, and advanced offerings.
key_actions.rationale: With 44% of clients willing to use managed services for digitization challenges, partnerships can accelerate CMIplus's ability to offer sophisticated solutions without extensive in-house development. This is crucial for expanding into complex data analytics, digital asset integration, and maintaining competitiveness against agile FinTechs.

key_actions.action: Define a clear vision for the future of cash management and the treasury function as a whole, and create momentum for change via senior-level leadership and advocacy.
key_actions.rationale: The scale of transformation described in the report requires a unified strategic direction for CMIplus. Clear vision and strong leadership buy-in are essential to navigate technological shifts, address talent gaps, and ensure that both clients and RBI employees understand and embrace the evolving role of cash management.

competitive_implications: The report underscores that FinTechs and non-traditional competitors are actively leveraging advanced technologies, posing a significant threat of commoditization for incumbent banks. CMIplus must proactively innovate and differentiate its offerings, particularly in data-driven services, industry-specific solutions, and digital assets, to maintain relevance and secure its position as a strategic partner for large international corporates in CEE.

case_studies.headline: Virtual Account Management (VAM) for customized reporting and control.
case_studies.key_achievement: Offers self-service tools to design and manage virtual account structures, centralizing treasury functions across multiple entities for customized reporting, control, and enhanced security.
case_studies.lesson: Virtual account management is a foundational element for advanced cash management, providing flexibility, control, and improved security, which CMIplus should prioritize for its corporate clients.

case_studies.headline: One Trade Multinacionales provides real-time insights into subsidiary accounts.
case_studies.key_achievement: Improves visibility and control for treasurers with real-time insights into subsidiary accounts across different markets, integrating with online banking systems and supporting payments via developer APIs.
case_studies.lesson: Real-time visibility across multi-currency accounts and robust API connectivity are crucial for international corporates, enabling better control and seamless integration with external financial ecosystems for CMIplus.

case_studies.headline: Citi Token Services for Cash: Blockchain-based digital asset solution for institutional clients.
case_studies.key_achievement: Enhances 24/7 cross-border liquidity and payments between branches, processing transactions on a private blockchain without requiring clients to hold or manage tokens, simplifying access and reducing operational complexities.
case_studies.lesson: Blockchain-based solutions offer significant potential for 24/7 cross-border liquidity and simplified digital asset access, which CMIplus should explore for future payment and settlement capabilities.

case_studies.headline: Enhancing freight payment processes with AI-based solutions.
case_studies.key_achievement: An AI-based solution accelerates payments and removes inefficiencies in legacy payment systems within the trucking industry, improving working capital for shippers and carriers.
case_studies.lesson: Industry-specific AI solutions can drive significant operational efficiency and working capital improvements for clients in specialized sectors, demonstrating the value of tailored, intelligent automation for CMIplus.

executive_summary: The 2025 McKinsey Global Payments Report highlights a payments industry at a critical juncture, shaped by geopolitical fragmentation, the rise of digital assets, and the transformative power of AI. While revenue growth is slowing to 4% annually through 2029 due to shifting payment methods and interest rates, payments remain highly valuable. The report outlines a future of competing systems and contested outcomes, emphasizing the need for players like CMIplus to embrace intelligent simplicity, robust interoperability, and programmable compliance. Success will hinge on adapting to a multirail ecosystem, leveraging AI for efficiency and new services, and building trust in an increasingly automated financial landscape. This requires strategic investment in agility, architecture, and trust to remain competitive.
key_stats: Global payments revenue increased 4% globally in 2024, a notable drop from 12% in 2023.
Total payments market size is projected to reach $3.0 trillion by 2029.
The payments industry generated $2.5 trillion in revenue from $2.0 quadrillion in value flows in 2024.
Payments gave an average 18.9% return on equity in 2024.
Cash usage declined to 46% of worldwide payments in 2024 (from 50% in 2023).
Account-to-account (A2A) payments now account for approximately 30% of global point-of-sale volume.
Stablecoin issuance doubled since early 2024, with daily transaction volumes around $30 billion.
10% of consumers use AI to start their online shopping journey, and 20% would be comfortable asking AI to make a purchase on their behalf.

themes.name: Payments Landscape Fragmentation & Regionalization
themes.description: The global payments ecosystem is becoming increasingly fragmented and regionally focused, driven by geopolitical events, national security priorities, and the proliferation of local payment systems (e.g., Pix, Bizum, UPI). This trend creates a complex environment with diverging standards, timelines, currencies, and trust anchors, moving away from a unified global system. CMIplus, operating across diverse CEE markets, must navigate this increasing fragmentation, adapting to regionalized systems while seeking opportunities for global passkeys.
themes.key_stat: The growing divergence in payments reflects the evolution of the broader financial system into a mosaic of regions with different standards, timelines, currencies, and trust anchors.

themes.name: Rise of Digital Assets and Tokenized Money
themes.description: Stablecoins and tokenized money are gaining significant traction, with issuance doubling since early 2024 and daily transaction volumes around $30 billion. Growing regulatory clarity (e.g., Genius Act in US, EU frameworks) and technological advancements are driving their adoption for real-world use cases, including instant cross-border payments, intraday returns on tokenized deposits, and programmable finance. This trend has the potential to disrupt traditional deposit funding and revenue models for financial institutions.
themes.key_stat: Stablecoin issuance has doubled since early 2024—but its role in the broader global payments landscape remains somewhat limited. With daily transaction volumes around $30 billion, stablecoins still represent a fraction of the trillions of dollars transacted worldwide each day.

themes.name: Transformative Potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
themes.description: AI is profoundly reshaping the payments landscape, enhancing efficiency and productivity across various functions. This includes transaction optimization (routing, settlement), software engineering (code generation, testing), and advanced risk and fraud management. The emergence of 'agentic AI,' where AI agents act autonomously to transact, is creating new competitive battlegrounds and will necessitate new approaches to payment orchestration and customer engagement.
themes.key_stat: 10 percent of consumers use AI to start their online shopping journey, and 20 percent would be comfortable asking AI to make a purchase on their behalf.

themes.name: Evolving Payments Revenue Models
themes.description: Global payments revenue growth is projected to slow to 4% annually through 2029, a notable drop from 12% in 2023. This deceleration is primarily due to peaking interest rates (slowing net interest income growth), a shift towards lower-cost payment options like account-to-account (A2A) transfers and digital wallets, and ongoing fee pressures. Payments players must adapt to new economic and fee models, especially as transaction volumes increasingly move to lower-yield rails.
themes.key_stat: Payments revenue growth slowed to 4 percent, a notable drop from the 12 percent increase in 2023.

themes.name: Interoperability as Core Infrastructure
themes.description: The future payments landscape will be defined by complex multirail and cross-border transactions. The report stresses that the ability to seamlessly bridge diverse asset types, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes in real-time will no longer be a differentiator but a fundamental requirement. Payments players must move beyond isolated systems and instead aim to become foundational layers within larger ecosystems, enabling others to build upon their intelligence, trust, liquidity, or connectivity.
themes.key_stat: Cross-border and multirail transactions will define any foreseeable future scenario. The ability to bridge asset types, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes in real time will no longer be a differentiator. Players will want adaptive infrastructure that supports this natively.

themes.name: Trust and Programmable Compliance
themes.description: As AI and automation increasingly initiate transactions, designing transparency, explainability, and error resolution into systems is paramount for building user and regulator trust. Concurrently, diverging regulations necessitate a shift towards programmable compliance, where modular policy engines and region-specific logic replace manual workflows and hard-coded rules. This approach is crucial for navigating fragmented global standards and ensuring secure, compliant operations across multiple jurisdictions.
themes.key_stat: As AI and automation increasingly initiate transactions, firms will want to ensure that transparency, explainability, and error resolution are designed into their systems, so that users and regulators can understand what happened and why.

key_actions.action: Enhance Multirail and Cross-Border Interoperability for CEE Corporates
key_actions.rationale: The report emphasizes a fragmented, multirail ecosystem. CMIplus, serving international corporates in CEE, must ensure seamless integration across diverse payment rails (EBICS, H2H, SWIFT, Open API) and jurisdictions, including emerging local schemes and instant payment networks. This is critical for maintaining competitiveness and offering comprehensive solutions to our clients.
key_actions.timeline: Ongoing, with immediate focus on API standardization and integration with new regional instant payment schemes in CEE.

key_actions.action: Integrate AI for Operational Efficiency and Value-Added Treasury Services
key_actions.rationale: AI is transforming transaction optimization, fraud detection, and reconciliation. CMIplus should leverage AI to automate manual workflows, enhance security for corporate clients, and explore agentic commerce capabilities for treasury management. This will reduce costs, improve service quality, and potentially create new revenue streams (e.g., AI-driven liquidity management, fraud analytics).
key_actions.timeline: Short-term (6-12 months) for initial AI-driven fraud detection and reconciliation pilots; Medium-term (1-2 years) for exploring agentic commerce and advanced liquidity management.

key_actions.action: Develop a Strategy for Digital Assets and Programmable Money Relevance
key_actions.rationale: Stablecoins and tokenized money are gaining regulatory clarity and real-world use cases, particularly for cross-border payments and programmable finance. CMIplus should assess the relevance of these technologies for its corporate clients in CEE, potentially exploring tokenized deposits or stablecoin-based cross-border settlement to offer new efficiencies and hedging options, while monitoring regulatory developments.
key_actions.timeline: Medium-term (1-2 years) for strategic assessment and pilot programs; Long-term (2-3+ years) for full integration based on market adoption and regulatory clarity in CEE.

key_actions.action: Codify Programmable Compliance and Embed Trust-by-Design Principles
key_actions.rationale: With diverging regulations and increased automation, CMIplus needs to build modular, region-specific compliance engines to ensure adherence to local policies across its network banks in CEE. Furthermore, embedding transparency, explainability, and error resolution into AI-driven processes is vital for maintaining corporate client trust and meeting regulatory scrutiny.
key_actions.timeline: Short-term (6-12 months) for reviewing existing compliance frameworks and identifying areas for modularization; Medium-term (1-2 years) for developing programmable compliance modules and integrating trust-by-design principles into AI solutions.

competitive_implications: The increasing fragmentation of payment systems and the rise of AI-driven agentic commerce will intensify competition, requiring CMIplus to evolve beyond traditional cash management to offer intelligent, ecosystem-embedded solutions. Failure to adapt to multirail interoperability, digital assets, and programmable compliance risks disintermediation by agile fintechs or larger platforms that control the 'edge' of payments, potentially eroding our market share among international corporates in CEE.

executive_summary: The "Journeys to Treasury 2025/26" report highlights a decade of treasury evolution, with a renewed focus on fundamental competencies like cash flow forecasting, systems, data, and skills. Digital transformation, driven by instant payments, ISO 20022, Verification of Payee (VoP), and AI, is reshaping the payment landscape and demanding real-time liquidity management. Treasurers are moving from reactive to strategic roles, leveraging automation and data analytics to enhance risk management, compliance, and decision-making. The emphasis is on building robust foundations and adopting technology incrementally to unlock long-term value and foster a culture of cash awareness across the business.
key_stats: 30.5% of treasurers prioritize cash flow forecasting the most.
27.3% of treasurers cite inaccurate forecasting as a leading challenge for centralisation.
38.5% of respondents cite difficulties in standardising processes as their most significant obstacle to centralisation.
38.7% of treasurers identify ESG reporting as their top regulatory concern.
27.6% of treasurers list fraud prevention as a priority.
17% of corporates now use virtual accounts primarily for reconciling incoming payments, up five to six percentage points from two years ago.
Over 93% of Comcast's accounts provide automated balance and statement reporting, and more than 80% of on-hand cash is now accessible by the corporate team.
Around 99% of Evonik's payment flows are now processed automatically.

themes.name: Return to Fundamentals & Cash Flow Forecasting
themes.description: Cash flow forecasting has re-emerged as the top priority for treasurers, driven by macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical uncertainty. Despite years of automation efforts, many models still rely on semi-manual processes, highlighting the need for reliable short-term and rolling forecasts. Accurate forecasting is crucial for working capital optimization, funding strategies, and risk management, underscoring the gap between intent and execution.
themes.key_stat: almost one in three treasurers (30.5%) prioritising forecasting the most.

themes.name: Payments Modernization (Instant Payments, ISO 20022, VoP)
themes.description: The EU Instant Payments Regulation, ISO 20022 migration, and Verification of Payee (VoP) are fundamentally reshaping the payment landscape. Corporates face new obligations, fraud risks, and system changes, but also opportunities for real-time liquidity management and accelerated receivables. Standardisation of data and processes is critical for navigating this complex, interconnected environment, with VoP becoming mandatory from October 2025.
themes.key_stat: From October 2025, the Instant Payments Regulation will also require a form of account name-checking known as verification of payee (VoP).

themes.name: Digital Transformation & Automation
themes.description: Treasurers are actively investing in technology upgrades, with a pragmatic focus on fixing core infrastructure before chasing the next wave of innovation like AI. The goal is to move beyond fragmented systems and manual processes towards integrated platforms that enable near-total payment straight-through processing, real-time dashboards, and automated workflows to free up time for strategic tasks. Legacy systems often block the adoption of the latest technologies.
themes.key_stat: reviewing and replacing treasury technology infrastructure is now the third-highest priority

themes.name: Real-time Liquidity & Visibility
themes.description: The pursuit of real-time liquidity has become a practical priority, moving beyond end-of-day snapshots to continuous, on-demand visibility into every account and transaction. This is enabled by APIs, virtual accounts, and integrated systems, allowing treasurers to base decisions on live data, respond to shocks as they unfold, and demonstrate control to stakeholders. Real-time information is no longer a luxury but a necessity for effective cash management.
themes.key_stat: Real-time information is no longer a luxury but a necessity for effective cash management.

themes.name: AI's Treasury Moment (From Hype to Hands-On)
themes.description: AI is transitioning from hype to practical application in treasury, with use cases emerging in forecasting, compliance, and workflow automation. Successful adoption relies on good, structured data, incremental implementation, and a focus on solving specific pain points rather than pursuing moonshots. AI is seen as an enabler to augment human judgment and free up time for strategic thinking, though treasurers are still in early stages of adoption.
themes.key_stat: the lower ranking of Al and blockchain suggests that treasurers are still in the early stages of adopting these more advanced tools,

themes.name: ESG Integration in Treasury
themes.description: ESG is no longer a parallel track but is becoming embedded in group finances, reporting, and long-term strategy, especially for Europe-headquartered companies facing growing regulatory obligations. Treasurers are transforming long-term loans into sustainability-linked structures and arranging green financing packages, positioning treasury as a strategic partner in sustainability efforts. ESG reporting is currently the primary driver of engagement.
themes.key_stat: 38.7% of treasurers identify ESG reporting as their top regulatory concern

key_actions.action: Enhance Real-time Data & Forecasting Capabilities for CEE Corporates
key_actions.rationale: Cash flow forecasting is the top priority for treasurers, and inaccurate forecasting is a leading challenge for centralisation. CMIplus must provide instant, granular visibility and predictive tools to help CEE corporates optimize liquidity and make faster, data-driven decisions, aligning with the 'real-time liquidity' theme.
key_actions.timeline: Immediate development and phased rollout over 12-18 months, focusing on CEE market specifics.

key_actions.action: Strengthen VoP and Fraud Prevention Features for SEPA and Cross-Border Payments
key_actions.rationale: VoP is mandated from October 2025, and fraud prevention is a top priority for treasurers. CMIplus must offer robust, seamless VoP integration, especially for multi-currency and cross-border payments in CEE, to reduce fraud and build trust. This includes supporting various identifiers and ensuring clear feedback mechanisms.
key_actions.timeline: Prioritize development for VoP compliance by Q4 2025, with continuous enhancements.

key_actions.action: Expand ISO 20022 & Open API Adoption and Guidance
key_actions.rationale: ISO 20022 is crucial for structured data and STP, and API fragmentation remains an obstacle. CMIplus should actively guide CEE clients on migration and leverage Open APIs for enhanced connectivity, real-time reporting, and integration with ERP/TMS systems, particularly for virtual accounts and multi-bank solutions. This addresses the need for standardisation and digital groundwork.
key_actions.timeline: Ongoing support and proactive client engagement, with new API features rolled out over 18-24 months.

key_actions.action: Develop AI-powered Treasury Assistants for CMIplus Users
key_actions.rationale: AI is transitioning from hype to hands-on, with use cases in forecasting and workflow automation. CMIplus can develop AI-powered virtual assistants for tasks like cash position queries, anomaly detection, and payment rule navigation, helping CEE clients reduce manual effort and gain insights, aligning with the 'AI's Treasury Moment' theme.
key_actions.timeline: Pilot projects in 12-24 months, broader rollout thereafter.

competitive_implications: Competitors are also focusing on real-time capabilities, AI, and regulatory compliance. CMIplus must differentiate by offering superior integration, user-friendly interfaces, and proactive guidance on complex regulations (VoP, ISO 20022) tailored to the CEE market. Failure to adapt rapidly risks losing market share to more agile fintechs and banks that embrace these transformations.

case_studies.headline: Dialling Up Cash Flow at Vodafone
case_studies.key_achievement: Transformed cash flow into a company-wide mission, embedding a cash-conscious mindset across all functions, leading to improved cash flow conversion and funding growth from within. Implemented receivables dashboards for real-time visibility.
case_studies.lesson: Cash flow transformation requires cultural change and cross-functional ownership, not just finance-only responsibility. Practical tools and granular data visibility drive positive developments and improve business performance.

case_studies.headline: From Complexity to Clarity: DEME's Evolving Treasury Journey
case_studies.key_achievement: Evolved from decentralised roots to a mature, centralised treasury function with a central payment factory and internal hub. Embedded sanctions screening earlier in the transaction lifecycle and transformed long-term loans into sustainability-linked structures.
case_studies.lesson: Centralisation and strong governance are crucial for control and efficiency as a business grows. Proactive risk management (e.g., early sanctions screening) and embedding ESG into financing are key strategic moves for modern treasury.

case_studies.headline: Treasury Automation in Action at Evonik
case_studies.key_achievement: Embedded automation at the core of operations, achieving near-total payment straight-through processing (99%) and real-time liquidity dashboards. Adopted SAP S/4HANA to unify systems and integrate seamlessly.
case_studies.lesson: Technology, particularly an integrated platform like S/4HANA, is a strategic partner for managing financial risks, optimising liquidity, and aligning with business goals. Automation frees up time for strategic decision-making.

case_studies.headline: Banking on Change: Inside Comcast's Treasury Transformation
case_studies.key_achievement: Overhauled a "Frankenstein" banking landscape into a unified global liquidity framework, closing over 2,000 bank accounts, consolidating with strategic partners, and making over 80% of on-hand cash accessible. Significantly reduced commercial paper borrowings.
case_studies.lesson: A multi-year, multi-continent treasury transformation requires strong executive sponsorship, clear core tenets, and a nuanced region-by-region approach to navigate logistical, regulatory, and cultural hurdles. It also develops talent and elevates treasury's strategic role.

case_studies.headline: Tackling Practical Questions in Verification of Payee's Rollout
case_studies.key_achievement: Actively engaged in assessing the impact of VoP, exploring practical ways to integrate verification results into ERP systems, and advocating for closer collaboration between banks, regulators, and technology providers.
case_studies.lesson: While VoP is a necessary step for fraud prevention, its rollout presents practical challenges for corporates, especially with name matching and integration into existing systems. Corporates need to be actively involved in shaping its evolution and push for better, harmonised solutions.

case_studies.headline: Racing the Clock and Winning! How Accell Group Built an In-House Bank in Just Three Months
case_studies.key_achievement: Responded to a crisis (product recall, excess inventory, credit rating downgrades) by designing and implementing a semi-automated in-house bank (IHB) in just three months, replacing a notional cash pool and restoring liquidity control.
case_studies.lesson: Under pressure, a lean, focused team with the right expertise and strong collaboration (internal and external) can achieve rapid, transformative results. Pragmatism and leveraging existing infrastructure are key to meeting tight deadlines.

case_studies.headline: Rewiring Treasury at Zoetis
case_studies.key_achievement: Built a lean, centralised, digitally enabled treasury function since its spin-off, achieving real-time cash visibility, automating reconciliation and reporting, and adopting end-to-end payment tracking via Swift GPI.
case_studies.lesson: Lasting treasury transformation begins with a clear vision rooted in real pain points, focusing on integration, data unlocking, and enhancing the team's ability to act on insights. Incremental progress and continuous evolution are more effective than waiting for a 'perfect roadmap.'
